name: Edu-ConvoKit
summary: A Python library from Stanford that annotates conversations in education: talk time, math vocabulary, student reasoning, focusing questions and how much teachers build on what students say.
grades: not stated (its classifiers were trained on 4th and 5th grade math lessons)

license.note: MIT covers the library. The classifiers it downloads from Hugging Face carry their own licenses, non-commercial or unclear (uptake-model, focusing-questions-model, student-reasoning-model). Its repository also holds samples of other datasets for its tutorials, under their own terms.

access_note: pip install edu-convokit. Version 0.4.0, the latest on PyPI, needs Python 3.10 or 3.11.
cite: Wang, R. E., & Demszky, D. (2024). Edu-ConvoKit: An Open-Source Library for Education Conversation Data. NAACL 2024 (System Demonstrations), 61-69. https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2024.naacl-demo.6

fits.how: Runs out of process over a learner's turns (integrations/stanford-edu-convokit): a measure gives talk time and math density with no model, and a detector marks reasoning, focusing questions and uptake with classifiers each person downloads.

connect.note: Writes the adapter. Install Edu-ConvoKit (Python 3.10 or 3.11) and start server.py; then viable-harness measure record.json --component measure.json gives the learner's share of the words and math terms per message. Its detector's classifiers come under their own terms, non-commercial or unclear. They learned from spoken classroom talk, and nobody has checked them on chats with an AI.
